hints: The graph starts at $(0, 15)$ and accelerates at $0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $30\text{ s}$ up to speed $15 + 0.4(30) = 27\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
The second stage is a horizontal line of duration $3T$ at constant speed $27\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from $t = 30$ to $t = 30 + 3T$.
The third stage decelerates at $0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for duration $T$, stopping before the time axis at point B.
walkthrough:
Identify the three straight-line segments between A and B:
1. Positive gradient segment from $(0, 15)$ to $(30, 27)$, since $v = 15 + 0.4(30) = 27\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
2. Horizontal constant speed segment at $v = 27\text{ m s}^{-1}$ lasting $3T$ seconds, from $t = 30$ to $t = 30 + 3T$.
3. Negative gradient segment of duration $T$, sloping downwards from $v = 27$ to $v_B = 27 - 0.2T$, ending above the time axis at $t = 30 + 4T$.
Label all key time and velocity coordinates on the axes: velocities $15, 27$ and times $30, 30 + 3T, 30 + 4T$.
teacher_walkthrough: Draw a velocity-time graph with velocity $v$ on the vertical axis and time $t$ on the horizontal axis.

Step 1: First phase ($0 \le t \le 30$):
Starts at point A with velocity $v = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t = 0$.
Uniform acceleration $a = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $30\text{ s}$:
$$v(30) = 15 + 0.4(30) = 15 + 12 = 27\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Plot a straight line with positive gradient connecting $(0, 15)$ to $(30, 27)$.

Step 2: Second phase ($30 \le t \le 30 + 3T$):
Constant speed of $27\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $3T$ seconds.
Plot a horizontal line segment from $(30, 27)$ to $(30 + 3T, 27)$.

Step 3: Third phase ($30 + 3T \le t \le 30 + 4T$):
Uniform deceleration of $0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $T$ seconds.
Velocity at B is $v_B = 27 - 0.2T$, which is positive.
Plot a straight line with negative slope connecting $(30 + 3T, 27)$ to $(30 + 4T, 27 - 0.2T)$ stopping strictly above the time axis.

ai_rubric.Sketching Motion Graphs: Draws three straight-line segments (positive slope to 27, horizontal segment, negative slope stopping above axis) with correct axis labels.

hints: Find the area under each section of the $v$-t graph: first trapezium $\frac{1}{2}(15 + 27)(30) = 630\text{ m}$, middle rectangle $27(3T) = 81T$, and third trapezium $\frac{1}{2}(27 + 27 - 0.2T)T$.
Sum the areas and set equal to the total distance $2750\text{ m}$: $630 + 81T + 27T - 0.1T^2 = 2750$.
Rearrange into the quadratic equation $0.1T^2 - 108T + 2120 = 0$ (or $T^2 - 1080T + 21200 = 0$) and solve for the valid value of $T$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area under each phase of the velocity-time graph:
Phase 1: $s_1 = \frac{1}{2}(15 + 27)(30) = 21 \times 30 = 630\text{ m}$
Phase 2: $s_2 = 27 \times (3T) = 81T\text{ m}$
Phase 3: $s_3 = \frac{1}{2}(27 + [27 - 0.2T])T = \frac{1}{2}(54 - 0.2T)T = 27T - 0.1T^2\text{ m}$

Set the sum of the areas equal to the total distance $2750\text{ m}$:
$$630 + 81T + 27T - 0.1T^2 = 2750$$
$$630 + 108T - 0.1T^2 = 2750$$
$$0.1T^2 - 108T + 2120 = 0$$

Multiply by 10 and factorize the quadratic equation:
$$T^2 - 1080T + 21200 = 0$$
$$(T - 20)(T - 1060) = 0$$

Choose the physical root:
For $T = 1060$, the velocity at B would be negative ($27 - 0.2(1060) = -185$), so $T = 20\text{ s}$.
teacher_walkthrough: The total distance travelled from A to B is given by the total area under the velocity-time graph, which equals $2750\text{ m}$.

Step 1: Calculate distance for Phase 1 ($0 \le t \le 30$):
This is a trapezium with parallel vertical sides $15$ and $27$ and width $30$:
$$s_1 = \frac{15 + 27}{2} \times 30 = 21 \times 30 = 630\text{ m}$$

Step 2: Calculate distance for Phase 2 ($30 \le t \le 30 + 3T$):
This is a rectangle of height $27$ and width $3T$:
$$s_2 = 27 \times 3T = 81T\text{ m}$$

Step 3: Calculate distance for Phase 3 ($30 + 3T \le t \le 30 + 4T$):
Initial speed is $27\text{ m s}^{-1}$, deceleration is $0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and duration is $T$.
The speed at B is:
$$v_B = 27 - 0.2T$$
The area is a trapezium:
$$s_3 = \frac{27 + (27 - 0.2T)}{2} \times T = \frac{54 - 0.2T}{2} \times T = (27 - 0.1T)T = 27T - 0.1T^2$$

Step 4: Combine all three areas and set equal to $2750\text{ m}$:
$$s_1 + s_2 + s_3 = 2750$$
$$630 + 81T + 27T - 0.1T^2 = 2750$$
$$630 + 108T - 0.1T^2 = 2750$$
Rearrange to standard quadratic form:
$$0.1T^2 - 108T + 2120 = 0$$
Multiply through by $10$:
$$T^2 - 1080T + 21200 = 0$$

Step 5: Solve the quadratic equation:
$$(T - 20)(T - 1060) = 0$$
This gives two mathematical roots: $T = 20$ or $T = 1060$.
If $T = 1060$, the car would have passed rest long before $t = 30 + 4T$ ($v_B = 27 - 0.2(1060) = -185\text{ m s}^{-1}$). Thus, the only physical root is:
$$T = 20$$

ai_rubric.Interpreting Motion Graphs: Forms total area expression $630 + 81T + 27T - 0.1T^2 = 2750$, sets up quadratic $T^2 - 1080T + 21200 = 0$, and rejects $1060$ to obtain $T = 20$.

hints: Calculate the speed of the car at point B using $T = 20$: $v_B = 27 - 0.2(20) = 23\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Use the suvat formula $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ from B to C with $u = 23\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $v = 0$, and $a = -0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Add the distance from B to C ($529\text{ m}$) to the distance from A to B ($2750\text{ m}$) to find the total distance from A to C.
walkthrough:
Find the speed at point B when $T = 20\text{ s}$:
$$v_B = 27 - 0.2(20) = 27 - 4 = 23\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the stopping distance from B to C under deceleration $a = -0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as \implies 0^2 = 23^2 + 2(-0.5)s_{BC}$$
$$0 = 529 - s_{BC} \implies s_{BC} = 529\text{ m}$$

Calculate the total distance from A to C:
$$s_{\text{total}} = s_{AB} + s_{BC} = 2750 + 529 = 3279\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the speed of the car at point B.
Using $T = 20\text{ s}$ found in part (b):
$$v_B = 27 - 0.2T = 27 - 0.2(20) = 27 - 4 = 23\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Step 2: Distance travelled during the final deceleration from B to C.
The car decelerates uniformly at $a = -0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ from initial speed $u = 23\text{ m s}^{-1}$ until coming to rest ($v = 0$):
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as_{BC}$$
$$0^2 = 23^2 + 2(-0.5)s_{BC}$$
$$0 = 529 - 1.0 s_{BC}$$
$$s_{BC} = 529\text{ m}$$

Step 3: Total distance from A to C.
The distance from A to B is given as $2750\text{ m}$:
$$s_{AC} = s_{AB} + s_{BC} = 2750 + 529 = 3279\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Constant Acceleration Formulae: Evaluates speed at B as $23\text{ m s}^{-1}$, calculates distance $s_{BC} = 529\text{ m}$, and sums to obtain $3279\text{ m}$.
